explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM and human judgments on the same instances using both agreement analysis (Cohen's kappa) and correlation analysis (Spearman correlation) of rankings, with detailed results across four criteria

prompts.notes: Prompt adapted from AlpacaEval benchmark and tailored to evaluation criteria, full prompt in Appendix D; jais-13B-chat excluded as judge due to failure to follow structured response guidelines

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Initial low agreement improved to sufficient level after adjudication

per_criterion.notes: Low initial agreement primarily due to borderline cases involving tie vs preference decisions

guidelines.notes: Detailed evaluation criteria described including pairwise comparison options and individual Tunisian Arabic usage scoring rubric (0-2 scale)

sample_size.notes: All 900 evaluation instances were evaluated by both human and LLM judges

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: not explicitly stated but values above 0.9 considered strong

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4o showed strongest alignment with human judgments (average Spearman correlation 0.9175) and was selected as primary automated judge; while ranking correlations were high, absolute agreement on Tunisian usage showed systematic overestimation by LLMs.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human judges evaluated the same four criteria using identical evaluation methodology
